title: [Accessibility] Login form uses GET method (defaults to GET, no method attribute)
body:
## Problem
The login form `<form>` tag lacks a `method` attribute, defaulting to GET. While JavaScript prevents the default submission and uses POST for the API call, the form element itself is semantically incorrect.

## Current State (app.js line ~722)
```html
<form class="login-page..." id="login-form">
```

## Issue
- No `method` attribute → defaults to GET
- No `action` attribute → submits to current URL
- If JavaScript is disabled, credentials would be exposed in the URL

## Required Fix
```html
<form class="login-page${isRegister ? ' register-mode' : ''}" id="login-form" method="post" action="/api/auth/login">
```

Note: Since the form uses `e.preventDefault()` and makes a fetch call anyway, this is primarily a semantic/accessibility fix. But adding `method="post"` ensures correctness.

## WCAG Standards
- **4.1.1 Parsing (Level A)**

## Priority: Medium

title: [Meta/SEO] All pages share the same title and meta description
[Meta/SEO] Missing Open Graph, Twitter Card, and canonical tags
body:
## Problem
The application lacks social sharing meta tags and canonical URL.

## Missing Tags
- `og:title` - Open Graph title
- `og:description` - Open Graph description
- `og:image` - Open Graph image
- `og:url` - Open Graph URL
- `twitter:card` - Twitter card type
- `twitter:title` - Twitter title
- `twitter:description` - Twitter description
- `canonical` - Canonical URL

## Required Fix
Add to `public/index.html` `<head>`:
```html
<!-- Open Graph -->
<meta property="og:title" content="IT Operations - Knowledge Base">
<meta property="og:description" content="IT Operations Knowledge Base - QA Library">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://your-domain.com">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">

<!-- Twitter Card -->
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">
<meta name="twitter:title" content="IT Operations - Knowledge Base">
<meta name="twitter:description" content="IT Operations Knowledge Base - QA Library">

<!-- Canonical -->
<link rel="canonical" href="https://your-domain.com">
```

## Priority: Low

title: [Security] HTTP headers: Referrer-Policy too strict, X-XSS-Protection disabled
body:
## Problem
Two HTTP security headers are suboptimal.

## Current State
```
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
X-XSS-Protection: 0
```

## Issues

### Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
- Too strict: no referrer info sent to ANY destination
- Breaks analytics, link tracking, and debugging
- Prevents referring site from knowing traffic source

### X-XSS-Protection: 0
- Disabled. While modern browsers rely on CSP instead, some older browsers still use this header.

## Required Fix
```
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
```

## Priority: Medium

title: [Security] Cache-Control set to max-age=0 for all static assets
body:
## Problem
All static assets (HTML, CSS, JS) are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0`, forcing a revalidation on every page load.

## Current State
```
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0
Last-Modified: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 18:02:58 GMT
ETag: W/"1187-..."
```

## Impact
- Every page load requires an HTTP request to check if content changed
- Increased latency and server load
- Poor performance on slow connections

## Required Fix
Serve static assets with appropriate cache headers:
```
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
```
For HTML (SPA shell):
```
Cache-Control: no-cache
```
Or use the existing Service Worker's stale-while-revalidate strategy more effectively.

## Priority: Medium

title: [UX] 404 page lacks useful navigation and error details
body:
## Problem
The 404 page is minimal - just a magnifying glass icon, "Page not found" text, and a single "Go to QA Library" button.

## Current State
- No explanation of what happened
- No search functionality
- No link to other main sections (Dashboard, Users, Sub-Systems)
- No back button to previous page

## Required Fix
Improve the 404 page with:
1. A brief explanation: "The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved."
2. Multiple navigation options:
   - Go to QA Library
   - Go to Dashboard
   - Go to Users
3. A "Back" button to return to the previous page
4. A search input to find content

title: [Security] X-Frame-Options and CSP: review frame-ancestors directive
[PWA] Service worker: no offline fallback for API routes
body:
## Problem
The service worker uses `network-only` for all API routes, meaning API calls fail completely when offline.

## Current State (sw.js)
```javascript
if (url.pathname.startsWith('/api/')) {
  event.respondWith(fetch(event.request).catch(() => new Response(null, { status: 503 })));
}
```

## Impact
- Users completely offline cannot see any cached data through API
- No optimistic UI updates possible when offline

## Required Fix
Consider implementing a cache-first or network-first strategy for read-only API routes (GET requests), while keeping write operations (POST/PUT/DELETE) as network-only.

## Priority: Low

title: [UI] Dark/Light mode toggle button icon is confusing
body:
## Problem
The theme toggle button uses emoji (☀️/🌙) which may not be clear to all users. The button shows ☀️ in dark mode (indicating "switch to light") and 🌙 in light mode (indicating "switch to dark").

## Current State
- Dark mode: button shows ☀️ (sun)
- Light mode: button shows 🌙 (moon)

## Issues
1. Emoji rendering varies across platforms (Windows vs macOS vs mobile)
2. The meaning is counter-intuitive (sun in dark mode = "go to light" but looks like it's showing "dark mode is on")
3. No tooltip explaining the action

## Required Fix
1. Use SVG icons instead of emoji for consistent cross-platform rendering
2. Add `title` attribute or tooltip:
   ```html
   <button aria-label="Toggle theme" title="Switch to light mode">☀️</button>
   ```
3. Consider using a more intuitive icon (e.g., a toggle switch)

## Priority: Low

title: [UI] Search input lacks visible label (only sr-only label)
body:
## Problem
The search input on Users page uses `class="sr-only"` for its label, making it invisible to sighted users. While the placeholder says "Search users...", relying solely on placeholder text is not best practice.

## Current State
```html
<label for="users-search" class="sr-only">Search users</label>
<input id="users-search" placeholder="Search users...">
```

## Issue
- `sr-only` label is only visible to screen readers
- Placeholder text disappears when user starts typing
- No visible label for keyboard-only users who tab through

## Required Fix
Make the label visible:
```html
<label for="users-search">Search users</label>
<input id="users-search" placeholder="Search users...">
```

Or use a visible search icon + label pattern consistent with the QA Library page.

## WCAG Standards
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A)**

## Priority: Medium
